## RESULTS (append; scripts t.py, t2.py)

result_text:
**Why conversion dropped:** a new landing page, `/lp/summer-sale`, started taking about 21% of sessions in the week of 06-08, and it converts far worse than the other pages. This is an association. Nothing in the data assigned traffic to that page at random, so it doesn't prove cause.

**Which metric I used.** Your 3.1% → 2.5% matches `checkout_reached` ÷ sessions: 131/4200 (3.12%) → 125/4971 (2.51%). Orders ÷ sessions gives 3.12% → 2.76%, so that isn't the metric you're quoting.

**Evidence**
- **The new page converts badly.** `/lp/summer-sale` didn't exist in week 1. In week 2 it brought 1,053 sessions and 6 checkout-reaches, or 0.57% (bootstrap 95% interval 0.19–1.04%). `/home` converts at 2.7% and `/product` at 3.8%. The new page was low on every day, including before the 06-10 deploy.
- **Everything else held steady.** On `/home` and `/product`, 131/4200 (3.12%) became 119/3918 (3.04%). The change was −0.86 to +0.67pp (95% interval), so zero is inside it. Almost the whole drop is the blended rate falling as low-converting sessions were added.
- **The v3.4.1 checkout refactor doesn't explain it.** I expected the 06-10 release to have hurt checkout. Existing-page conversion was 3.00% on 06-08/09 and 3.05% on 06-10 to 06-14. The change was −1.16 to +1.12pp (95% interval). This test can't detect a drop smaller than about 1pp, so a small refactor effect isn't ruled out. The new page was already at about 0.6% before the release, so there is no step at 06-10.
- **Session logging has a gap.** On 06-13 and 06-14 session rows drop to about 585 a day, against 760 on 06-08 to 06-12. Orders on those days (23 and 17) exceed the sessions that reached checkout (17 and 11) by 6 each, which suggests about 350 sessions are missing. Adjusting for that gives about 2.58%, so the gap explains only about 0.07pp of the 0.6pp drop. I can't tell why the rows are missing, and there is no independent session count to check against.

**Limitations**
- Orders don't carry a session ID, so I couldn't measure conversion per page from orders. Per-page numbers use `checkout_reached`.
- The new page's sample is small (6 conversions), so its exact rate is uncertain. It is clearly well below the other pages.
- I didn't check whether the new page's weakness comes from its traffic source, its content, or its checkout path. Nothing in this data separates those.
- I only partly tested whether a shift in device mix mattered. Desktop's share of sessions rose from 44% to 49%, which looks driven by the new page's traffic. I didn't test desktop on the old pages separately.
- The skill file cut off mid-sentence in its Data section (line 221), so I didn't see its remaining guidance on interval checks. I used bootstrap intervals throughout.

**What to do.** Look at whether `/lp/summer-sale` traffic is the wrong audience or the page has a problem, and don't roll back v3.4.1 on this evidence. Ask whoever owns logging about the 06-13/14 gap.
